sources.entry: ai-evaluation - Open-source LLM evaluation framework with 50+ metrics, LLM-as-Judge, guardrail scanners (jailbreak, PII, injection), and AutoEval pipelines with CI/CD support.

summary.one_liner: Agent Learning Kit is a local-first Python SDK and CLI (with a TypeScript evaluation package) for simulating, evaluating, red-teaming, and optimizing AI agents, from the Future AGI project that also hosts the ai-evaluation code.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes three engines: simulate (local worlds, tasks, framework adapters, replays, regression artifacts), evals (evaluating prompts, task outputs, runtime contracts, traces, memory, retrieval, safety and robustness evidence), and optimize (searching over prompts, agents, workflows, memory layers and red-team scenarios). Red-teaming is run on top of the simulate and evals engines through a campaign command. The CLI (agent-learn) provides eval, run, optimize, redteam, doctor, release-check and release-proof commands that write JSON artifacts. A harness under src/fi/alk/harness reads an agent's source, builds a world for its tools, and writes test scenarios, driven from a terminal or a local web chat on port 8777. The README states that everything in the quickstart runs offline without an API key, with optional Future AGI platform mode.
use_cases: test an AI agent offline before release
evaluate LLM prompt and response quality
red-team an agent with adversarial scenarios
optimize prompts or agent workflows and compare candidates
replay agent runs as regression tests in CI
check retrieval, memory, and tool-use behavior of agents
notable: Harness that points at an agent's source and generates proved test scenarios, usable from a terminal or a local web chat
Single artifact model: simulate, evaluate, optimize, and promote results into replayable artifacts
Offline quickstart with bundled example manifests and no API key required
Framework adapter probes for LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, AutoGen, CrewAI, MCP, A2A and others
Release-proof command that emits command evidence for the full local test and build stack
caveats: The README says the TypeScript npm package publishes only at the v1 launch; today it must be built from source
Some framework coverage is described as probe-promoted or runtime-simulated rather than full support
Platform-backed evaluation requires a Future AGI API key; the default mode is local-only
